description: The name Exocraft combines exo—looking beyond our home planet—with craft—the art of precision engineering and problem-solving. Whether we are mapping distant worlds or monitoring Earth from orbit, we build tools designed for discovery.
summary: EXOCRAFT: CHRONO-TWIN is an interactive Google Maps-style discovery tool which combines open-source data for Earth, Moon, and Mars provided by NASA and world space agencies. We have developed a multi-planetary mapping tool, which allows simultaneous viewing of planetary features on all worlds using our newly discovered Tri-Planetary Thermal-Diode Connection. This connects broken, basaltic lava tubes and volcanic skylights on Earth, (Umm Jirsan, Saudi Arabia), Moon, (Marius Hills) and Mars, (Alba Mons). Users can view rock, dune and crater features in detail across Earth, Moon and Mars. We provide live information about mineral content, oxygen, weather conditions and soil toxicity. Users can toggle between Ancient Wet Mars and Modern Arid Mars. We also provide backwards search functionality to identify risks to spacecraft failure. CHRONO-TWIN reduces risk to missions by using multi-dimensional similarity analysis with a clear log of Where the Analogy Breaks Down. This increases pre-flight hardware testing and prepare us for long term exploration on the Moon and Mars.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

At its core, EXOCRAFT: CHRONO-TWIN is designed to display three separate worlds (Earth, The Moon & Mars). Zoom and pan to view any area of your choice. There is also a toggle switch that allows you to view different worlds or worlds together. You can also zoom and pan across areas of interest such as the Umm Jirsan lava tubes, Rub’ al Khali mega dunes, Danakil hydrothermal plains, Marius Hills skylights or Alba Mons/Jezero Crater fissures. You can click on individual rocks, boulders, dunes and craters. When clicking on any surface feature you will see EXOCRAFT: CHRONO-TWIN open up a dynamic Rock and Surface Composition Inspection Tool. This will show you what the macrotexture looks like (with an example illustration), what type of rock it is, what percentage of minerals are present from a chemical perspective and if it’s fertile or toxic from a soil perspective. Comparing Earth’s organic carbon content and extremophile microbes with Mars’ perchlorate content and the Moon’s electrostatic regolith. This will also generate a dynamic Analog Similarity Percentage which compares the amount of Oxygen, air pressure, wind speed, current Earth weather, temperature variation, water/ice state and subsurface geology.

Creative & Scientific Elements

I made sure this tool was very creative and scientific by designing it around a new Tri-Planetary Thermal Diode Connection. Showing how broken lava tubes and volcanic skylights on Earth, The Moon and Mars act as thermal buffers protecting the interior from extreme temperatures outside whilst ensuring volatiles remain trapped underneath. I have also included a Planetary Time Period Toggle so you can compare Earth locations to Ancient Wet Mars (3.5 Billion Years Ago) or Modern Arid Mars. There is also a Reverse Hardware Failure Finder where you can see what type of failure a particular spacecraft may encounter due to certain conditions such as electrostatic dust blockages or jagged basalt wheels. I made sure this tool was scientific by providing a Where The Analogy Falls Short section. This shows when the actual data from orbit is being used compared to when an example has been used for educational purposes. This also highlights the limitations of Earth such as one G gravity, high air pressure, different cosmic radiation and terrestrial contamination.

Benefits, Impacts & Tools Used

EXOCRAFT: CHRONO-TWIN takes disparate satellite data of different planets and turns it into an easy to understand visual lab. This reduces costs of testing hardware in the field before launch. Preventing hardware failures on alien surfaces. This provides a way to easily research planetary analogues for students, engineers and new space programmes worldwide. I created this web application using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, React, Tailwind CSS, Interactive Canvas, SVG Mapping and Netlify. I incorporated free data from NASA LRO (WAC, LOLA, Diviner), NASA MRO (HiRISE, CRISM), Viking MDIM 2.1, NASA EMIT, SMAP, SRTM, MODIS, Esri World Imagery, NASA Planetary Fact Sheets and the Open-Meteo Live Weather API.
